\section*{Executive summary and current status}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Executive summary and current status}
For a map pixel \(p\), SCI-MAP forms the coefficient-weighted average
\begin{equation}
 \widehat x_p=\frac{\sum_iG_{pi}\omega_i x_i}
                         {\sum_iG_{pi}\omega_i}
 =\frac{N_p}{Q_p},
 \label{eq:map}
\end{equation}
using only calibrated samples with valid coordinates, upstream eligibility,
and finite positive effective coefficients. Here \(G_{pi}\) describes how
sample \(i\) is assigned or divided among pixels, and \(\omega_i\) is the
upstream-declared analysis coefficient. Pixels without adequate valid support
are unavailable; they are not measurements of zero sky brightness.

For compatible observation maps on one common grid, the v0.1 coadd is
\begin{equation}
 \widehat s_p=\frac{\sum_o u_{op}\widehat x_{op}}
                         {\sum_o u_{op}},
 \label{eq:coadd}
\end{equation}
where every admitted observation coefficient \(u_{op}\) is finite and
positive. An observation is not partly coadded: its signal, coordinates,
response, uncertainty, validity, and provenance must be mutually compatible
before it contributes.

Both equations are linear only \emph{conditional on fixed} sample and detector
membership, projection, coefficients, support policy, response state,
geometry/WCS, calibration, and upstream processing. If any of those states is
estimated from the same data, unconditional bias or covariance requires a
joint model or resampling result.

\StatusBox{\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}L{0.31\linewidth}Y@{}}
\textbf{Intended scientific estimator} & Positive-coefficient ordinary map and compatible common-grid observation coadd, Equations~\eqref{eq:map}--\eqref{eq:coadd}.\\
\textbf{Upstream input status} & Inherited conditionally from SCI-CAL, ALIGN/AST, PTC, and VAL; unresolved \code{xs}, broadband, calibration, response, or uncertainty status is not repaired by MAP.\\
\textbf{Implementation conformance} & Not assessed in this authorship revision.\\
\textbf{Response/representation validation} & Not established; response injections and WCS round trips remain required evidence.\\
\textbf{Observational validation} & Not established; amplitude, shape, position, covariance, and repeatability require astronomical controls.\\
\textbf{Production readiness} & Not claimed and cannot be inferred from the algebraic contract.\\
\end{tabularx}}

\tableofcontents

\clearpage
\section{What SCI-MAP estimates}\label{sec:estimand}
SCI-MAP estimates a map-domain average of the \emph{calibrated, processed}
sample quantity. It does not estimate unconvolved sky truth. The physical
meaning of the result is therefore inherited from the complete upstream
chain: what the ordinary \code{xs} sample represents, how it was calibrated
and conditioned, what sky coordinate it has, and which samples are eligible.

The numerical signal scale may be the declared point-source-equivalent
\(\mjybeam\) convention inherited from SCI-CAL. MAP does not create absolute
calibration, choose a beam convention, or complete an unresolved broadband
photometric definition. A numerical map may consequently exist while literal
point-source-peak interpretation remains unavailable because the response for
the declared processing chain is incomplete. The same caution applies to
extended-source fidelity, integrated flux, and absolute offsets.

The map response is the full upstream sky-to-sample response followed by the
map operator. In compact notation,
\begin{equation}
 \widehat{\boldsymbol x}=A\boldsymbol y,\qquad R=AH,
 \label{eq:response}
\end{equation}
where \(H\) maps a declared sky model into processed samples and \(A\) maps
those samples into valid pixels. Preserving a constant \emph{sample vector}
does not prove preservation of a constant sky mode: an upstream baseline,
common-mode removal, or filter may already have removed it.

A stored kernel is a realized response only when its template, sample-domain
parent, and processing lineage prove the relation in Equation~\eqref{eq:response}.
Otherwise it is a tracer or has an explicit unavailable status. Every
response-dependent consumer must retain that distinction.

\hfill\(\longrightarrow\)\hfill

\clearpage
\section{From samples to pixels}\label{sec:samples}
For each candidate sample \(i\), the projection coefficient \(G_{pi}\) is the
assignment or fraction by which that sample contributes to pixel \(p\).
One-hot projection has one nonzero \(G_{pi}=1\). Fractional projection may
divide a sample among neighboring pixels. Any other projection class must be
explicitly authorized rather than inferred from array shape or a software
default.

The coefficient \(\omega_i\) comes from PTC. The approved PTC authority calls
these scalar analysis and gridding coefficients and requires their family,
units, normalization scope, lifecycle, and applied factors to be declared.
They may be uniform, detector-based, sample-based, sensitivity-derived, or
another named family. They are not inverse variances merely because their
stored unit is inverse-square signal. A stronger precision interpretation
requires separate calibration and covariance/independence evidence.

The effective contribution is \(G_{pi}\omega_i\). SCI-MAP first selects the
samples whose calibration, coordinates, flags, signal, projection, and
required companions are valid, then accumulates
\begin{equation}
 N_p=\sum_iG_{pi}\omega_i x_i,\qquad
 Q_p=\sum_iG_{pi}\omega_i.
\end{equation}
The numerator is not yet a sky estimate, and the denominator is a gridding
normalization by default. Division occurs only where the adopted support
policy permits a scientific map value.

Whether a fractional projection must conserve every interior sample through
\(\sum_pG_{pi}=1\), how boundary loss is represented, and which non-one-hot
classes are allowed are not fixed by the admitted upstream authority. They
are therefore recorded as SCI-MAP-OD-008 rather than hidden behind the symbol
\(G\). Until resolved, every product must declare its actual projection and
boundary convention, and no unrecorded conservation property may be assumed.

\section{Projection, response, and correlated pixels}\label{sec:projection}
Fractional projection is useful because a sample can represent support that
overlaps more than one pixel. The same operation also carries the sample's
noise into each recipient pixel, correlating them.

\begin{figure}[h]
\centering
\fcolorbox{MapNavy}{MapPale}{\parbox[c][0.52in][c]{0.14\linewidth}{\centering\small sample}}
\quad
\begin{minipage}[c]{0.24\linewidth}\centering
\(G_{p1}=1/2\;\nearrow\)\\[0.30em]
\(G_{r1}=1/2\;\searrow\)
\end{minipage}
\quad
\begin{minipage}[c]{0.18\linewidth}\centering
\fcolorbox{MapBlue}{white}{\parbox[c][0.35in][c]{0.82\linewidth}{\centering pixel \(p\)}}\\[0.18em]
\fcolorbox{MapBlue}{white}{\parbox[c][0.35in][c]{0.82\linewidth}{\centering pixel \(r\)}}
\end{minipage}
\quad
\parbox[c]{0.28\linewidth}{\small The same noise realization enters both pixels, so \(\operatorname{Cov}(\widehat x_p,\widehat x_r)\ne0\).}
\caption{A fractionally projected sample creates shared noise support.}
\label{fig:split}
\end{figure}

For a concrete calculation, take two independent samples of equal variance,
each split equally into the same two pixels, with \(\omega_i=1\). In either
pixel, \(Q=1/2+1/2=1\), but
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Var}(\widehat x_p)=
 \frac{(1/2)^2+(1/2)^2}{Q^2}=\frac12,
 \qquad \phi_p=\operatorname{Var}(\widehat x_p)^{-1}=2.
\end{equation}
Thus normalization is 1 while formal marginal inverse variance is 2. The two
pixels are also correlated because each contains both sample errors. This is
why projection, normalization, formal precision, and full covariance must be
separate products.

\clearpage
\section{Weights and uncertainty}\label{sec:uncertainty}
For fixed upstream and map state, uncertainty propagates through the same map
operator as the signal:
\begin{equation}
 C_x=A N A^{\mathsf T},
 \label{eq:cov}
\end{equation}
where \(N\) is the processed-sample noise covariance. Equation~\eqref{eq:cov}
retains cross-pixel terms created by shared samples and any correlations
already present in the timestream.

Four quantities answer different questions:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(Q\): the gridding denominator that normalizes the map;
\item a formal marginal inverse variance: valid only under its stated
coefficient and covariance assumptions;
\item the full conditional map covariance or precision, including correlated
pixels when available; and
\item empirical covariance, weights, or statistical significance calibrated
by NOI from admitted realizations or data.
\end{enumerate}

The raw map bundle must say whether covariance is persisted, recoverable from
lineage, summarized, or unavailable. It must not turn missing correlations,
calibration uncertainty, astrometric uncertainty, response uncertainty, or
additive-bias uncertainty into zeros. A signal multiplied by the square root
of a merely formal weight is a \emph{formal standardized signal}, not an
empirical significance map.

The distinction is especially important when sample membership, weights,
projection, response, or support is estimated from the same observation. The
linear equations remain useful conditional descriptions, but they do not
include selection uncertainty. A joint model, resampling study, or other
separately justified treatment is needed for an unconditional statement.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering\small
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}L{0.26\linewidth}L{0.20\linewidth}Y@{}}
\toprule Quantity & Owner/status & Science interpretation \\
\midrule
Analysis coefficient \(\omega\) & PTC, declared scalar family & Gridding/analysis coefficient; precision only if separately proved.\\
Normalization \(Q\) & MAP & Denominator of the ordinary estimator; not automatically uncertainty.\\
Conditional covariance & PTC input, MAP propagation & Fixed-state error covariance through projection and normalization.\\
Empirical weight/significance & NOI & Requires declared realizations, calibration, and validity evidence.\\
Calibration/response nuisance & SCI-CAL and response owner & Retained as quantified, lineage-resolvable, or unavailable; never silently zero.\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\caption{Ownership prevents a convenient numerical product from acquiring a stronger statistical meaning.}
\end{table}

\clearpage
\section{Coverage, support, and validity}\label{sec:validity}
The formal contract keeps eight facts separate. For science users they answer
the following questions:
\begin{longtable}{L{0.43\linewidth}L{0.25\linewidth}L{0.23\linewidth}}
\toprule Science question & Product & Interpretation \\
\midrule
Did projected samples geometrically reach this pixel? & Geometric hits & Geometry, not estimator admission.\\
How many valid weighted samples entered the estimator? & Accepted estimator hits & Exact contribution count.\\
How many complete observations entered this coadd pixel? & Contributing observation count & Observation bundles, not samples.\\
What detector-time was available before estimator-specific rejection? & Upstream-eligible exposure & Eligible detector-time accounting.\\
How much detector-time was retained by the estimator? & Retained exposure & Retained accounting, not precision.\\
Was the denominator large enough to normalize? & Numerical support & Lower support threshold.\\
Is the pixel inside the adopted science region? & Science-policy support & Stricter policy threshold.\\
Is the complete raw map value scientifically usable? & Final map validity & Required conjunction of identity, support, finite value, companions, and no product failure.\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

Hits are not validity, exposure is not precision, and positive normalization
is not sufficient for final validity. A rectangular FITS image may contain
storage values outside the scientific domain; the explicit support and
validity products determine which pixels are measurements. Unsupported pixels
are unavailable, not zero sky.

\PolicyBox{\textbf{Provisional two-threshold policy.} A lower threshold permits
numerically safe normalization; a stricter threshold defines the adopted
science region. Both are scaled from an order statistic of the finite positive
normalizations in a declared map population. This is adopted policy, not a law
of mapmaking or a proof of completeness, response, or noise quality.}

Because the reference normalization is computed from a declared population,
changing the map extent or population can change the science mask even when
the local samples near a particular pixel are unchanged. That global behavior
must be justified and validated for the intended use.

The formal equations compare \(Q_p\) with \(Q_\star c/10\) and \(Q_\star c\).
Dimensional consistency therefore forces \(c=\texttt{coverage\_cut}\) to be
dimensionless. The current normative r0.1 clauses incorrectly leave its unit
status open. SCI-MAP-CI-001 records the inconsistency and proposes the exact
owner amendment; no normative clause is changed before approval. The allowed
numeric domain and behavior for negative, zero, non-finite, or greater-than-one
values remain open in SCI-MAP-OD-007.

\clearpage
\section{Observation coaddition}\label{sec:coadd}
V0.1 combines observation maps only when they already represent the same
responded quantity on the same pixel grid. Each observation contributes as a
complete bundle: signal, normalization, response state, covariance status,
exposure, support, validity, WCS, and provenance are checked together.

The permitted placement is a centered integer embedding. A smaller map may
sit inside a larger common grid only when each dimension differs by a
nonnegative even number of pixels; half the difference is the integer offset.
The shifted reference pixel must identify the same world coordinate. An odd
shape difference is incompatible and the complete observation is rejected.
There is no fractional shift, interpolation, reprojection, or implicit
recentering in this ordinary branch.

\begin{figure}[h]
\centering
\begin{minipage}[c]{0.18\linewidth}\centering
\fcolorbox{MapBlue}{MapPale}{\parbox[c][0.48in][c]{0.82\linewidth}{\centering observation 1\\complete bundle}}\\[0.22em]
\fcolorbox{MapBlue}{MapPale}{\parbox[c][0.48in][c]{0.82\linewidth}{\centering observation 2\\complete bundle}}
\end{minipage}
\hfill\(\longrightarrow\)\hfill
\fcolorbox{MapGold}{MapGoldPale}{\parbox[c][1.18in][c]{0.22\linewidth}{\centering identity, WCS, shape\\unit, response, validity\\uncertainty, provenance}}
\hfill\(\longrightarrow\)\hfill
\fcolorbox{MapNavy}{white}{\parbox[c][1.18in][c]{0.15\linewidth}{\centering centered\\integer\\common grid}}
\hfill\(\longrightarrow\)\hfill
\fcolorbox{MapBlue}{MapPale}{\parbox[c][1.18in][c]{0.20\linewidth}{\centering coadd signal/response\\covariance/exposure\\validity/observation count}}
\caption{Complete-bundle admission and centered-integer placement. Any failed compatibility check rejects the observation before it contributes.}
\label{fig:coadd}
\end{figure}

This restriction is the declared scope of the ordinary v0.1 coadd, not a
general scientific argument against mosaicking. Whether observation maps are
cropped or padded upstream to a canonical grid, and which future package owns
reprojection or mosaicking, are not fixed by the admitted authority and are
recorded as SCI-MAP-OD-009. Until then, SCI-MAP performs neither operation.

The coadd propagates response and conditional covariance through the same
observation membership and placement. Its denominator is again normalization,
not automatically precision. Correlated generalized least squares, which may
need negative coefficients and a full cross-observation covariance, belongs
outside this positive-coefficient branch.

\section{Units, WCS, products, and downstream use}\label{sec:products}
SCI-MAP preserves the scale, unit convention, response basis, validity, and
uncertainty status supplied by SCI-CAL. It preserves the coordinates, exact
frame metadata, geometry, and coordinate validity supplied by ALIGN/AST; it
does not replace that authority with the shorthand phrase ``J2000.'' PTC owns
the processed sample and coefficient/covariance inputs, and VAL owns upstream
sample and detector eligibility. MAP transforms these inputs but does not
complete, repair, reinterpret, or validate them.

The accepted map-bundle authority is ADR~0009 and its 2026-08-05 owner
amendment. The full binary64 typed or sidecar WCS is the lossless identity used
for admission, common-grid comparison, and provenance. The WCS serialized in
the FITS product is the representation ordinary scientific tools are expected
to use for pixel-to-sky conversion. It must preserve axis sign, handedness,
orientation, and the exact centered-integer reference-pixel relations, and
must agree with the lossless authority within 0.1 arcsec maximum sky
separation. The bound is cited from that owner-approved representation
authority; this rationale does not invent a physical justification for it.

The FITS product remains scientifically self-describing at its declared
serialization fidelity, while the sidecar retains exact identity for
conformance, provenance, and coadd admission. A tolerance never authorizes a
different sky grid, fractional shift, interpolation, or reprojection.

\begin{longtable}{L{0.36\linewidth}L{0.54\linewidth}}
\toprule Science-user state & Interpretation and required action \\
\midrule
Valid map; response available & Use only for the response class and processing lineage actually declared.\\
Valid numerical map; response unavailable & Restrict to owner-approved response-independent uses; response-dependent consumers fail closed.\\
Formal weight; empirical significance unavailable & Use as declared formal normalization/precision only; do not call it significance.\\
Covariance summarized or unavailable & Do not make a claim that needs missing correlations or nuisance terms.\\
Unsupported pixel & Unavailable, not zero sky.\\
Raw-invalid pixel & No downstream finite value may promote it to raw-valid.\\
Coadd-incompatible observation & Entire observation bundle is excluded; no partial coadd.\\
WCS or unit incompatibility & Reject combination rather than silently convert, recenter, or relabel.\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

Downstream packages inherit the raw unit, response, covariance, validity, WCS,
and provenance. NOI owns empirical noise and significance; FLT owns filtered
response, covariance, and validity while preserving the immutable raw parent;
source, Pointing/OOF, and Beammap packages own their scientific inference.

\clearpage
\section{Validation}\label{sec:validation}
Validation must keep algebra, software conformance, representation fidelity,
observational performance, and production readiness separate. The required
science program is:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{\arabic*.},leftmargin=*]
\item analytic estimator tests for constants, unequal coefficients, and exact
hand calculations;
\item one-hot and fractional projection tests for response, formal variance,
and cross-pixel covariance;
\item support, boundary, global-population, and unsupported-pixel tests;
\item complete-bundle compatibility and centered-integer coadd placement
tests;
\item sequential/parallel conformance: floating results agree within a
preregistered bound appropriate to operation count and conditioning, while
identities, counts, masks, support, offsets, and product cardinality agree
exactly;
\item synthetic point, extended, gradient, edge, and variable-coverage
response tests; and
\item observational amplitude, shape, position, covariance, and repeatability
checks against independent references.
\end{enumerate}
No test, implementation inspection, reduction, or production qualification
was executed for this authorship revision.

\section{Open scientific decisions}\label{sec:decisions}
The compact register in Appendix~\ref{app:decisions} preserves OD-001 through
OD-007 and appends OD-008 and OD-009. The new items expose genuine upstream
gaps rather than asking implementation questions. SCI-MAP-CI-001 separately
records the pending dimensional correction for \code{coverage_cut}; approval
would narrow OD-007 to numerical domain and failure behavior.

After r0.2, the planned remaining editorial work is one scientific-owner and
voice review. Further revisions should follow an owner decision, a normative
contract change, new validation evidence, or a newly identified scientific
inconsistency--not stylistic churn.

\section{Document authority}
Rationale revision r0.2 changes genre, teaching order, and ownership clarity.
It does not change the 52 canonical requirements, 25 canonical predictions,
or the v0.1 estimator. The exact threshold equations and \code{coverage_cut}
clauses remain unchanged pending owner approval of SCI-MAP-CI-001. The formal
contract and engineering conformance specification remain the normative
authorities for audit, repair, re-audit, and exact product behavior.
